page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD hardware. It provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It operates on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features no bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-threaded performance contrasted with limited aggregate parallel throughput due to the dual-thread configuration. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance scored 3746.07, positioning in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded compression also demonstrated upper-tier capabilities, recording 40.52 GB/sec in gzip compression and 18.03 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, parallel workloads are constrained by the two vCPUs: multi-core stress-ng registered at 3755.57 and the PassMark CPU score reached 5089.01, both placing in the bottom 25%. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 43.28 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 33.7 GB/sec, placing in the middle 50%.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio and robust per-thread execution speed, the E2as_v7 is operationally suited for small in-memory caches, lightweight database services, single-threaded processing pipelines, and development environments requiring substantial memory headroom per compute unit. Workloads demanding parallel throughput, intensive local disk I/O, or dedicated accelerator pipelines are poorly matched to its hardware envelope.
description: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of 4.5 GHz. Configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, it exhibits top-tier single-core compute and data decompression capabilities, evidenced by high single-core stress-ng and gzip compression results. However, aggregate multi-threaded capacity and total throughput metrics fall into lower percentiles due to the 2-vCPU core limitation. Memory throughput maintains average rates for large block reads and writes. The E2as_v7 fits memory-intensive applications requiring low aggregate thread counts, such as lightweight in-memory databases, Redis caches, and single-threaded batch tasks.
